newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SOCCER-BURMA OPEN TIGER CUP CAMPAIGN IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BURMA OPEN TIGER CUP CAMPAIGN IN STYLE.

text.p: Burma opened their Tiger Cup campaign in style on Thursday with a comprehensive 5-0 win over neighbours Cambodia.
But one of the tournament favourites, Vietnam, struggled and had to settle for a 1-1 draw with Laos.
Burma, coached by former Red Star Belgrade player Ratomir Dujkovic, opened the scoring in the 14th minute through Tin Myo Hung.

Win Aung added the next two goals, one either side of halftime, before Myo Hliang Win, tipped to be one of the outstanding players of the tournament, scored the fourth in the 71st minute. Maung Maung Oo bagged the fifth on the stroke of full time.
Vietnam, silver medallists in last year's Southeast Asia Games, were rattled by the Laotians, who lost their opening Tiger Cup match 5-1 to Indonesia.

Vietnamese defender Huu Thang was sent off in the 34th minute for his second bookable offence, and seven minutes into the second half, Laos's libero Luang Amath Chalana took advantage of the extra man to give his side the lead.
The visitors pressed Laos for most of the second half but were repeatedly denied by goalkeeper Soulivanh Xuenivilay.
But five minutes before time, Le Huynh Duc, top scorer in the Vietnam league this year, equalised to give his side a point which leaves them top of their group.
